correctness.rationale: The exact RK4 interval and q=13 switch check out, but the Finding (RESULT.md line 29) additionally asserts strict improvement over forward Euler for every allowed d,q. At q=2 the graph has degree d, Θ=2d and the proved sharp horizon H_{d,2}=H3=1/d equals the forward-Euler horizon. For example H(3,2) has both endpoints 1/3. This falsifies the stated universal strict inequality; equality occurs for all q=2 and the strict comparison holds for q≥3. For the main interval I rebuilt the off-diagonal coefficients independently from signed moments of the commuting clique spectral projectors. The distance-two coefficients after homogenization on [0,H3] are positive; for distance one all but the last are positive and its sign at d=3 is the sign of 64−5q, with a positive-coefficient certificate when d≥4. Descartes on the transformed polynomial gives the unique exceptional zero, and the distance-three entry is strictly negative for every h>H3. The diagonal is positive by the scalar fourth-order Taylor remainder and spectral resolution; distances above four are structural zeros, not active boundary zeros. For the strict Euler comparison in the exceptional q≥13 case, the adjacency coefficient of A is positive at Euler's horizon and the other coefficients are nonnegative (the A³ coefficient is zero there, not strictly positive as claimed in the proof). The scaled limiting cubic and the example roots agree. Replay exact shell and sign checks with python /workspace/branches/math_checks.py 1; the frozen checker and notes were inspected, not run. This is a completed-step result, not stage positivity.
